pr_title: GDScript: Add errors when calling unimplemented virtual functions
pr_body:
This PR does a small refactor of how method flags are handled in the GDScript analyzer. This way, it adds support for the analyzer to use any of MethodInfo's flags, where previously it could only use `METHOD_FLAG_STATIC` and `METHOD_FLAG_VARARG`.

As a side-effect, this also normalizes behavior between editor and release templates, which fixes #76938. The error is not exactly the same, as I didn't want to make changes to core, but it should be functionally similar:

**Editor:**

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/1133892/f1c49ef5-02d7-4f8e-9327-7f52165b3a24)

**Template release:**

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/1133892/977e7ca5-8c65-4895-b5dc-f37ac72a39ff)


Also works with an extra layer of indirection, with behavior similar between `editor` & `template_release`:
```GDScript
class TestZero:
	func _init():
		pass
	
class TestOne extends TestZero:
	pass

class TestTwo extends TestOne:
	func _init():
		super()
```


The tests added also brought a different issue to light, where using `super()` appears to generate a return variable discarded on calling super's _init(), which doesn't have a return value. This should be tackled in a different PR, which will have to change the output of this PR's tests.

issue_context.title: super() causing script error when overriding _init() on the child class and not the parent in release builds
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.3, 4.1-dev1, 4.1-dev2

### System information

Windows 11, ASUS Zephyrus G14 2022, Ryzen 9, Radeon 6700S

### Issue description

If you create a custom class script and extend it in a custom sub class script using GDScript, override `_init()` in the sub class but not in the parent class, and then call `super()` in the sub class, it will run fine in the editor or if exported with the debug template. However, if you export a release build, the `super()` call will induce a script error.

I think the bug is that the debugger should throw an error in this case. Trying the same with methods like `_ready` for classes extending nodes or even `_to_string` for a RefCounted class and running in the editor will cause a script error to be caught by the debugger.

In editor:
![debug](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/125445387/f6da77c5-c9d3-4bb9-a4b0-80d2f9218033)

Release build:
![release_error](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/125445387/73a9d098-7c3b-45e4-8761-e3f40ffd3bc9)


### Steps to reproduce

Create two classes
ClassTwo extends ClassOne
ClassTwo overrides virtual method _init() (**ClassOne does not**)
ClassTwo calls super() in _init()
No error in debug/editor
Error in release

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
I'm looking into this one :)

The cause of the issue is in `ClassDB::get_method_info()`, in the following part of the code:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/809a98216267f3066b9fec2f02b2042bdc9d3e0d/core/object/class_db.cpp#L515-L538

The `DEBUG_METHODS_ENABLED` flag enables a check for virtual methods, whereas without that flag, as in `template_release`, no such check is done.

I believe the error in `template_release` is correct and should be replicated in the editor. The analyzer should be able to tell us whether, when calling `super()`, there are no actual implementations of the method.
Reopening as #77324 was partially reverted by #78533.

Did some testing to better understand the problem, so we can find the right solution.

We should keep in mind that `_init` is a pretty special function which is implemented differently from regular virtual methods. Likewise, virtual callbacks like `Node._ready()` are also special. Then we have "normal" virtual methods defined by the user in a class and overridden in another. None of these are directly related to `virtual` C++ methods in the class implementation (though sometimes the GDScript / scripting API "virtual" methods do match a C++ virtual method).

I think it's important to test all three types of "scripting bindings virtual" methods to get a good picture of what works and what doesn't.

Notably I noticed that the behavior with `_init()` described here is not reproducible with `_ready()`, nor with a custom virtual method, which also behaves differently from `_ready()`.

---

Testing project, using Godot 4.0.3-stable:
[TestGDScriptVirtual.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11824465/TestGDScriptVirtual.zip)

It has a structure with `class_name C` extending `class_name B` which extends `class_name A`. I added `B` in the middle for testing with no overrides, to make sure calls probably bubble up the inheritance chain.

```gdscript
class_name A
extends Node

# Comment those in turn to test different scenarios.

func _init():
	print("init A")

func _ready():
	print("ready A")

func my_virtual():
	print("virtual A")
```

```gdscript
class_name B
extends A
```

```gdscript
class_name C
extends B

func _init():
	super()
	print("init C")

func _ready():
	super()
	print("ready C")
	
	my_virtual()

func my_virtual():
	super()
	print("virtual C")
```

### Removing `A._init`

When commenting out `A._init`, I get:

- In the editor: No error/warning
- Running from the editor: No error, it runs without issue
- Running with a release template:  Parse error in terminal:
```
SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Function "_init()" not found in base B.
          at: GDScript::reload (res://C.gd:5)
```

### Removing `A._ready`

When commenting out `A._init`, I get:

- In the editor: No error/warning
- Running from the editor: Runtime error in debugger:
```
Invalid call. Nonexistent function '_ready'.
0 - res://C.gd:9 - at function: _ready
```
- Running from a release template: Parse error in terminal:
```
SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Function "_ready()" not found in base B.
          at: GDScript::reload (res://C.gd:9)
```

Note how the behavior differs here when running from the editor (`DEBUG_ENABLED` build)

### Removing `A.my_virtual`

When commenting out `A.my_virtual`, I get:

- In the editor: Parse error in script editor (and in terminal):
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/983f0272-b9c1-4b48-87e3-f8423524fece)
```
SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Function "my_virtual()" not found in base B.
          at: GDScript::reload (res://C.gd:15)
```
- Running from the editor: Same parser error, also in debugger this time.
- Running from a release template: Same parser error, in terminal only.

Super thorough and super interesting! There are so many ways in which virtual functions can exist!

Right now this is feeling relatively similar to what already happened in #64253, where we had to essentially unify information stored in debug and non-debug builds (so more stuff ended up stored in release builds) basically so that the GDScript compiler is allowed to _not_ throw errors when attempting to typecheck something related to, in this case, virtual methods in release builds.

I'll test my current solution, which once again is about storing extra info in non-debug builds, in different builds against the examples you've given above and report back when I've got time.

It is annoying that we are increasing runtime memory usage for the sake of validating scripts which should a-priori already be known to work.

If my findings are correct that `_init` is the only virtual method with this problem, we could add a special case for it instead of embedded info on all virtual methods in release builds. But there might be other reasons why virtual method info could be needed in release builds.

I think it makes a lot of sense to check whether we can replicate this outside of `_init`, because if it truly is this localized, i.e. only happens on `super()` inside `_init()`, then we can probably target it directly.

I have to run now, but the case that comes to mind is extending existing core classes and using `super()` in our implementations of virtual methods. For example:
```GDScript
class D extends Node:
	
	func _process(delta):
		super(delta)
```

I'll try to test these later! Gotta run right now :)

review_comments:
I wanted to bring attention to this. I removed this line entirely, because it seems to me that the static information should already be coming from `function_signature_from_info()`, and the tests pass without this.

So either the test coverage isn't good enough, or this was redundant!

It looks like it's the same thing.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/49243a9a9816b334002f7d73d9e940d00b49158d/core/variant/variant_call.cpp#L1344-L1349

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/49243a9a9816b334002f7d73d9e940d00b49158d/core/variant/variant_call.cpp#L1405-L1407

I figured so too, but because this part of core is pretty foreign to me, I don't know whether it checks for a few more things that `function_signature_from_info()` might not. So at least it's documented here as a possibility.
